title: Area, Lattice Points, and Exponential Sums
relevant_concepts: Bombieri-Iwaniec method (Farey dissection, resonance curves, double large sieve)
structural ceiling: perfect spacing cannot get the zeta exponent below 3/20
notes: London Mathematical Society Monographs 13, Oxford, 1996. The monograph of the Bombieri-Iwaniec method. The ceiling statement used by docs/theory/exponent_pair_two_monomial.md and docs/problems/juggler_bi_resonance_limit.md: even a complete resolution of both the first and second spacing problems cannot get the zeta exponent below 3/20 = 0.15 (recorded in the Encyclopedia of Mathematics entry 'Bombieri-Iwaniec method' and in Huxley's survey 'Integer points in plane regions and exponential sums'; the survey also places the method's working middle range at log M/log T near 1/2 with Sargos's 1995 variant near 2/5). On the BI line q = p + 1/2 the zeta exponent equals the pair coordinate p, so no BI-producible pair has p < 3/20.
